items.prompt: A task was completed on Monday (status DONE, completedAt Monday 09:00). On Tuesday an edit form sends { "status": "DONE", "priority": "HIGH" }. What completedAt does TasksService.update write?
items.answer: Monday 09:00, the value it already had
distractors: Tuesday's save time, a fresh new Date()
null, as completedAt is reset on each save
No completedAt key, since status is unchanged
items.explanation: With dto.status DONE and before.status DONE, the inner ternary selects before.completedAt, so the Monday value is written back. Writing new Date() was the original bug.

items.prompt: A legacy row is DONE but has completedAt null. A client sends { "status": "DONE" }. What completedAt goes into the update data?
distractors: The current time, backfilled
The row's createdAt time
The row's updatedAt time
items.explanation: A repeat DONE reuses before.completedAt whatever it holds, so null stays null. The guide calls repairing such rows a separate data decision.

items.prompt: A DONE task with completedAt T1 is reopened with { "status": "OPEN" }. What does the status branch write?
items.answer: status OPEN with completedAt set to null
distractors: status OPEN, and completedAt is kept as T1
status OPEN, with no completedAt key at all
status OPEN, and completedAt is set to now
items.explanation: Any supplied status other than DONE takes the outer else branch of the ternary and writes completedAt: null, the existing convention for leaving DONE.

items.prompt: A DONE task receives { "priority": "HIGH" } and nothing else. What keys are in the data passed to prisma.task.update, and is an audit row written?
items.answer: Only priority, and one task.updated audit row is still written
distractors: priority and completedAt: null, then a single audit row
priority, status and completedAt, plus one task.updated row
Only priority, and no audit row is written, since status did not change
items.explanation: With no status the spread contributes {}, so only line 64 adds a key. The audit call after the update runs unconditionally, so a task.updated row is inserted anyway.

items.prompt: A client sends { "status": null } for a DONE task. What happens, given that @IsOptional() lets null through validation?
items.answer: The status branch is skipped; no status or completedAt is written
distractors: Prisma rejects status: null, and the request then fails with a 500 error
The task becomes OPEN, and completedAt is cleared to a null
A 400, as the DTO rejects null for its status enum field
items.explanation: null is falsy, so dto.status ? ... : {} contributes nothing. The guide warns that "tidying" the check to !== undefined would instead pass status: null to Prisma and produce a 500.

items.prompt: A client sends { "assigneeId": "" } to PATCH /api/tasks/:id. What does the update data contain for assigneeId?
items.answer: assigneeId: null, which unassigns the task
distractors: No assigneeId key, as an empty string is falsy
assigneeId: "", stored as an empty string
A 400 error, since an empty id is not a string
items.explanation: Line 65 is a presence check (dto.assigneeId !== undefined), so the empty string enters the branch, and dto.assigneeId || null turns it into null.

items.prompt: A client sends { "status": "DONE", "completedAt": "2020-01-01T00:00:00Z" } trying to backdate a completion. What happens?
items.answer: A 400 from the global pipe, before the controller runs
distractors: The key is stripped silently, and the rest of the update proceeds
completedAt is set to 2020-01-01 as the client asked
The service ignores the key but logs it in the audit
items.explanation: main.ts installs ValidationPipe with whitelist and forbidNonWhitelisted. completedAt is not a property of UpdateTaskDto, so the request is rejected with 400; it never reaches the service.

items.prompt: Writer A reads an OPEN task at line 52 and pauses. Writer B then completes it with { "status": "DONE" } at time T1. A resumes and also sends DONE, saving at time T2. What completedAt is stored at the end?
items.answer: T2, because A decides from its stale OPEN read
distractors: T1, since the second DONE is treated as a repeat
null, as two DONE writes cancel each other out
T1, because Prisma rejects A's stale update
items.explanation: A's before still says OPEN, so it takes the "entering DONE" path and writes new Date() (T2). The update has only where: { id } and no version check, so nothing detects the race.

items.prompt: An edit changes only a task's dueAt. What do the before and after objects of the resulting task.updated audit row contain?
items.answer: Only status and priority, which are unchanged here
distractors: Only dueAt, the one field that actually changed
status, priority and dueAt, before and after
Every column of the task row, before and after
items.explanation: The audit call always records { status, priority } for before and after. dueAt, assigneeId and completedAt are never in the audit payload, so this row shows no visible difference.

items.prompt: prisma.task.update succeeds, but the following audit.log insert throws. What state is the task left in?
items.answer: The task change stays committed without its audit row
distractors: Both are rolled back by the surrounding transaction
The task update is retried until the audit succeeds
The task change is undone by a compensating update
items.explanation: The audit write is a separate awaited call after the update, not inside prisma.$transaction. Once the update has committed, an audit failure cannot undo it.

items.prompt: In the vm-loaded test, assert.deepEqual(data, { priority: "HIGH" }) fails even though data holds exactly that. Why does test 3 compare Object.keys(data) instead?
items.answer: Objects made in the vm context have a different Object.prototype
distractors: data is a Prisma proxy object, so deepEqual cannot read its keys
deepEqual compares Date fields by reference rather than by value
The audit double mutates data after update has recorded it
items.explanation: The service runs in a separate vm realm, so its objects carry that realm's prototype, and deepEqual reports "same structure but not reference-equal". Arrays from Object.keys are built in the test's realm.

items.prompt: Someone "fixes" the bug by always writing before.completedAt whenever status is DONE. Which test catches it, and how?
items.answer: Test 2: IN_PROGRESS to DONE writes null, so getTime() throws
distractors: Test 1, since a repeat DONE now writes the fixed clock time instead
Test 3, because data gains a completedAt key
None of them, since all three still pass
items.explanation: Test 2 moves a task from IN_PROGRESS (completedAt null) to DONE and expects the fixed clock instant. Reusing before.completedAt writes null, and calling getTime() on it throws.

items.front: What are the four status cases TasksService.update distinguishes for completedAt?
items.back: Entering DONE from another status: new Date(). Repeating DONE: keep the existing value. Leaving DONE (any other status): null. Omitting status: neither status nor completedAt is in the payload; absent is different from null, which would erase history.

items.front: Why is a repeat DONE save not "idempotent", even though completedAt no longer changes?
items.back: Each request still bumps Task.updatedAt (Prisma @updatedAt) and inserts a new task.updated audit row. Say precisely which field is stable rather than calling the whole endpoint idempotent from one assertion.

items.front: Why should you not change dto.status ? ... to dto.status !== undefined ? ... while fixing completedAt?
items.back: @IsOptional() lets null through, so { "status": null } currently skips the branch. A presence check would pass status: null for a required enum, which Prisma rejects as a 500. Leave unrelated conditions alone until the new contract is decided and tested.

items.front: What does the focused completion test suite NOT prove?
items.back: Decorators are stripped and DTO, Prisma and audit are stubs, so it proves nothing about HTTP validation, dependency injection, authentication or SQL. The e2e file covers only health, so no automated test sends a real PATCH /api/tasks/:id.
